 Follow Truck driver arrested in KC area for safety violations. Then he was stopped again
 Nathan Pilling Fri, November 20, 2026 at 9:46 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. A Louisiana semi driver was pulled over twice in a three-day span last month and found with a swath of safety violations on Platte County roadways both times, the Platte County Sheriff’s Office said. A Louisiana truck driver was pulled over twice on Platte County roadways over a three-day span last month and found with a swath of safety violations both times, the Platte County Sheriff's Office said.
 The driver, identified in court documents as Alexander Hollier, was arrested and faces a series of charges after the stops.
 Initially, a deputy pulled over the driver of a tractor-trailer who was hauling an oversized load on Interstate 29 around 8:30 p.m. Oct. 27. The vehicle was traveling in darkness, with cargo that was hanging several feet off each side of its trailer and wasn't displaying an oversized load banner or warning devices, according to court documents.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The truck had an expired registration plate, and the driver had an expired commercial driver's license, the deputy wrote in court documents.
 The sheriff's office said the driver also didn't have an international fuel tax agreement license, a logbook or an oversized load permit from the state. In total, the deputy found eight violations of federal safety regulations.
 The deputy checked a federal registry and also found the man's company, Southern Motor Freight LLC, had an inactive safety registration status with the U.S. Department of Transportation.
 The two traffic stops came several days before a fatal crash involving another semi truck on U.S. Highway 71 in Kansas City in which two children and a mother were killed, and several others were seriously hurt. Police have alleged that truck driver was speeding and had a tablet open to YouTube before the crash.
 Truck driver charged in Platte County
 The driver told the deputy he had picked up his cargo in Iowa and was hauling it to Louisiana. Pictures that the Platte County Sheriff's Office posted on social media showed the truck was transporting farming and mowing equipment.
 Advertisement Advertisement Platte County prosecutors charged the man with four misdemeanors for the width and length of his vehicle, driving without a valid commercial license and failing to keep a driver record.
 The man posted bond, and two days after the arrest, the same deputy saw the same truck and driver on Missouri Highway 92, again with its oversized load, the sheriff's office said. The vehicle had warning devices and banners in place, but the deputy was aware that the driver still did not have a state permit and pulled the truck over again, the post said.
 The driver had obtained a valid commercial driver's license but still didn't have the needed state permit. This time, 15 federal safety violations were found, the sheriff's office said.
 The driver was issued a citation for the width of his vehicle, and the sheriff's office assisted the man with obtaining the state permit, the post said.
